text:
mira (eng-security): Heads-up — our nightly backup uploader started putting objects into s3://redwood-archive-int WITHOUT the SSE-KMS header. Noticed this in the recent integrity audit.
jon (eng-sre): whoa. any pattern? specific prefix / time range?
taylor (backup-service): starts 03:02 UTC tonight, all uploads from backup-worker-12. I sampled one object:\n```\n$ aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-archive-int --key nightly/db/2026-03-20/backup-2026-03-20-0302.snappy\n{\n  "ContentLength": 134217728,\n  "ContentType": "application/octet-stream",\n  "Metadata": {},\n  "ServerSideEncryption": "AES256"\n}\n```\nThat AES256 is SSE-S3, not SSE-KMS. We should have been using the tenant CMK for these snapshots.
carla (db-eng): Was there a deploy/role change to the uploader role recently? KMS grants can be sensitive to IAM edits.
mira (eng-security): Yes — ops merged a minimizing PR to backup-uploader role yesterday to tighten S3 list perms. I suspect the change removed kms:GenerateDataKey usage on the CMK grant path. Opening audit logs next.
encops-bot: :rotating_light: 3 objects missing SSE-KMS detected by encryption-audit (rule:s3-sse-check) | correlation id: enc-audit-20260320-0306
jon (eng-sre): Mira — can you query CloudTrail for PutObject events from backup-worker-12 around 03:02? If PutObject didn't include x-amz-server-side-encryption, it implies the client didn't request KMS.
mira (eng-security): On it. Quick grep shows PutObject calls with no SSE headers and IAM principal arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/backup-uploader/backup-worker-12.\ncloudtrail snippet:\n```\nuserIdentity: { "arn": "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/backup-uploader/backup-worker-12" }\neventName: PutObject\nrequestParameters: { "x-amz-server-side-encryption": null }\n```\nSo uploader didn't request KMS. That suggests the client fallback used SSE-S3 because uploader code hits s3lib default.
taylor (backup-service): I just checked the last deploy: a change in the uploader's config removed the env var REDWOOD_SSE_TYPE (defaulting to AES256 now). We rolled that change as part of a permission hardening PR to the role's assume-policy — the code change was intended to be harmless.
carla (db-eng): So two orthogonal changes coincided: role PR and config PR. Need to decide remediation: restore SSE-KMS for existing objects (re-encrypt) or mark them and rotate/expire? Also must fix uploader to use SSE-KMS and ensure it has KMS perms.
mira (eng-security): Action items I propose: 1) immediate hotfix: redeploy uploader with REDWOOD_SSE_TYPE=aws:kms and point at the correct CMK ARN; 2) create temporary KMS grant for the backup-uploader role to allow kms:GenerateDataKey/kms:Encrypt for canary restores; 3) run a canary restore of one affected snapshot to validate decrypt path; 4) run an inventory query to list objects missing SSE-KMS and tag them for follow-up. Agree?
jon (eng-sre): +1 for hotfix. I can roll a config-only deploy in 10m. For the KMS grant, use a least-privilege grant limited by encryption context (if we include tenant id). Example CLI to create a grant: \n```\naws kms create-grant --key-id alias/tenant-archive-cmk --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-uploader --operations Encrypt GenerateDataKey --constraints EncryptionContextSubset={"tenant":"tenant-42"}\n```\nThat grant expires when manually revoked; good short-term fix.
taylor (backup-service): I'll prepare the redeploy and add a config check in CI so REDWOOD_SSE_TYPE can't be removed silently. Also adding an integration test that asserts s3 put includes SSE header.
carla (db-eng): For existing objects, we should NOT auto-reencrypt in-place — that risks integrity mismatches and race conditions. Better plan: copy affected objects to a new key with SSE-KMS and then update manifest pointers. We'll do a single-tenant canary copy first.
mira (eng-security): Agreed. I'll open a ticket and update the snapshot/restore runbook with steps to verify SSE headers during upload and to query CloudTrail mapping for PutObject events. Also adding a post-deploy monitoring rule to alert if >1% of backups in a 1-hour window lack SSE-KMS.
encops-bot: ticket created: ENC-7123 "archive uploader removed SSE-KMS — remediation runbook" | assigned: taylor, mira | priority: high
jon (eng-sre): After redeploy, I'll run this query to find affected keys: \n```\naws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket redwood-archive-int --prefix nightly/db/2026-03-20/ --query "Contents[?ServerSideEncryption!='aws:kms'].Key" --output text\n```\nThen we'll iterate copy+tag for a small set and do a canary restore.
taylor (backup-service): Rolling the config-only deploy now. I'll post back when it's up and point to the redeploy commit.
mira (eng-security): Thanks. Long-term we need two follow-ups: (A) IAM review — ensure backup-uploader role has explicit kms:GenerateDataKey on archive CMKs (via grant or policy), and (B) telemetry: add a token-level telemetry point in uploader to emit chosen SSE mode and CMK id into our tracing/metrics.
carla (db-eng): Also recommend a pre-deploy linter that fails if SSE env var removed from templated helm values for backup chart.
jon (eng-sre): Deploy finished, uploader now sends SSE-KMS again. Running list query now.
taylor (backup-service): quick status: created grant ID abcdef12-3456-7890 and started canary copy of 3 objects into s3://redwood-archive-int-encrypted/; will attempt restore from copy in 30m.
mira (eng-security): Great. I'll coordinate a postmortem once we have restore results. For now mark incident as in-progress and don't escalate externally.
carla (db-eng): If canary restore succeeds, we'll schedule a controlled re-encrypt for the rest with a maintenance window.
jon (eng-sre): Result: canary restore successful, files decrypt with tenant CMK. I'll attach logs to the ticket.
mira (eng-security): Closing loop — created follow-up tickets for IAM policy check (ENC-7124) and telemetry change (ENC-7125). Thanks team :thumbsup:
